author: Caleb Stipkovits
title: Cedars at Pier One recovering from break-in attempt - NewsBreak
text:
By Caleb Stipkovits ,
5 hours ago The Brief • At least five Kennewick businesses have been targeted by vandalism and break-ins within one week
• Cedars at Pier One restaurant suffered $5,000 in damage when vandals smashed windows and chairs through their patio area
• Kennewick police are offering extra patrols to concerned businesses, but owners worry it may not be enough
KENNEWICK, Wash. — A wave of vandalism and break-ins has struck at least five Kennewick businesses in just one week, leaving owners frustrated and concerned about their security.
Cedars at Pier One restaurant on Clover Island became one of those victims last Thursday night, when it appears vandals attempted to break into the establishment.
Restaurant co-owner Doug Lundgren discovered the destruction when he arrived at work last Friday morning.
"I had broken windows at the restaurant, chairs scattered all over the patio, I had damaged tables," Lundgren said.
Cedars already had several security measures in place, including indoor security cameras and an alarm system that would have triggered if someone had fully broken through the windows. Still, even those safety measures weren't able to stop the vandals, who caused nearly $5,000 in damages.
The incident has left Lundgren wondering why someone would choose to attack his business.
"You feel violated. You feel for no apparent reason whatsoever. If it was just vandalism, I don't understand that at all. For break in, well, maybe someone was after something," he said.
The restaurant represents one of five Kennewick businesses targeted during this troubling week-long crime spree, creating anxiety among local business owners.
Lundgren and his co-owner had actually been proactive about security after hearing about other attempted break-ins in the area. They decided to order an outdoor camera for their patio, but the vandalism occurred before the equipment arrived.
In response to the recent break-ins, Kennewick police have told businesses they can request extra patrols if they feel concerned about their security. However, Lundgren worries that it may be hard to increase patrols for every worried business owner.
"I don't feel ok. Yes, extra patrols would be great, just as a deterrent... but they can't be here 24 hours a day. They got other things to do. More important things to do too," he said.
The financial impact of these crimes extends beyond just the immediate repair costs. For businesses already facing economic challenges, unexpected expenses from vandalism and break-ins can create additional strain.
Cedars at Pier One was able to quickly repair the damage, and will remain open during its regular hours of 4 p.m. to 9 p.m., Tuesday through Sunday.
The attempted break-in at Cedars is still under investigation by local authorities.
